summary: Apple iOS, macOS, and other Apple products contain a user-after-free vulnerability that could allow a malicious application to elevate privileges.

title: CVE-2025-23006: SonicWall SMA1000 Appliances Deserialization Vulnerability

title: CVE-2020-11023: JQuery Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability
summary: JQuery contains a persistent cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability. When passing maliciously formed, untrusted input enclosed in HTML tags, JQuery's DOM manipulators can execute untrusted code in the context of the user's browser.

title: CVE-2024-50603: Aviatrix Controllers OS Command Injection Vulnerability

summary: Microsoft Windows Hyper-V NT Kernel Integration VSP contains a use-after-free vulnerability that allows a local attacker to gain SYSTEM privileges.

title: CVE-2025-21333: Microsoft Windows Hyper-V NT Kernel Integration VSP Heap-based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

title: CVE-2024-55591: Fortinet FortiOS and FortiProxy Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
summary: Fortinet FortiOS and FortiProxy contain an authentication bypass vulnerability that may allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to gain super-admin privileges via crafted requests to Node.js websocket module.

title: CVE-2023-48365: Qlik Sense HTTP Tunneling Vulnerability
summary: Qlik Sense contains an HTTP tunneling vulnerability that allows an attacker to escalate privileges and execute HTTP requests on the backend server hosting the software.

Supreme Court: Andrew v. White
summary: At the time of the decision of the Oklahoma Court of Criminal Appeals, clearly established federal law provided that the erroneous admission of unduly prejudicial evidence could render a criminal trial fundamentally unfair in violation of due process, see Payne v. Tennessee, 501 U. S. 808, 825 (1991); the judgment below is vacated and the case is remanded for further proceedings. (No. 23-6573, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 604 U.S. 86).

title: Supreme Court: TikTok Inc. v. Garland
summary: The challenged provisions of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, 138 Stat. 955, do not violate petitioners’ First Amendment rights. (No. 24-656, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 604 U.S. 56).

title: Supreme Court: E.M.D. Sales, Inc. v. Carrera
summary: The preponderance-of-the-evidence standard applies when an employer seeks to demonstrate that an employee is exempt from the minimum-wage and overtime-pay provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act. (No. 23-217, opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 604 U.S. 45).

title: Supreme Court: Royal Canin U. S. A. v. Wullschleger
summary: When a plaintiff amends her complaint to delete the federal-law claims that enabled removal to federal court, leaving only state-law claims behind, the federal court loses supplemental jurisdiction over the state claims, and the case must be remanded to state court. (No. 23-677, opinion by Justice Kagan; 604 U.S. 22).
